analysis.title: GS Blekos - US Kickstart / GOAL Positioning / Global Servers / Munich RE / Swiss RE / SES / A&D / Eutelsat / Drax
key_insights: US Weekly Kickstart: after months of interest-rate pressure, concerns about the rising cost of capital have led the equity market to downgrade its growth expectations. A sharp reduction in investor positioning has amplified equity market moves.
GS baseline embeds slowing but still solid growth in 2027. Adjusted for accounting distortions, S&P 500 EPS growth is expected at 29% in 2026 and 18% in 2027.

GS recommends consumer-facing laggards for a catch-up, and a screen of defensive stocks with quality attributes for investors worried about a further catch-down. The base case macro outlook points to real income growth accelerating in 2027, particularly for the lowest-income consumers.
GOAL Positioning: the cross-asset sentiment and positioning indicator fell to the 46th percentile, its lowest level since April, decoupled from continued strong Global PMIs.

The largest drags on the positioning indicator are stronger fixed income fund flows (Exhibit 12), a sharp decline of the Risk Appetite Indicator below zero, and increased positioning in traditional safe havens (Gold, JPY).
Global Servers: general server value raised by 17% in 2027 and 11% in 2028E, with both shipments and ASP raised. General server shipments are expected to grow 20% / 12% / 8% YoY in 2026-28E.

Global Servers: AI server (NVL72, powered by NV and AMD) shipments raised by 5% / 1% to 110k / 164k racks in 2027 / 28E. AI server (8-GPU, powered by GPU and ASIC) shipments raised by 10% / 29% to 2.7m / 3.3m servers in 2027 / 28E. Better mix and higher memory costs drive CSP spending.
Munich Re reports 3Q'26 on November 12. GS net result estimate is 1% below company-collected consensus, with a c.3% lower technical result broadly offset by a higher investment result.

Munich Re: GS P&C Re combined ratio estimate of 79.2% is c.1.8ppts less favourable than consensus, mainly because of a higher nat cat estimate. The normalised combined ratio is expected to be in focus: GS 82.5% vs consensus 82.4%, consistent with management commentary pointing to further upward pressure from the c.82% reported at 2Q'26.

Swiss Re reports 3Q'26 on November 5. GS net income estimate is 18% below company-collected consensus, driven by a higher nat cat estimate and an assumption that management keeps building resilience through reserve additions and realised investment losses. The 2026 earnings trajectory remains on course to exceed the $4.5bn target.

SES SA: rating reinstated at Buy with a EUR 7.0 price target. Shares have doubled then halved within a year. After disappointment on C-band timing and weak 2Q results, GS sees an attractive entry point with asymmetric upside from incoming C-band cash and higher space-defence spend.

SES: the price target is described as conservatively discounting both opportunities and still offers 79% upside. A blue-sky scenario, where concerns about the scale and timing of benefits ease, implies more than 180% upside.

Europe Aerospace & Defense: GS sees Buy-rated Rheinmetall (on Conviction List) as the most compelling opportunity to capture structurally higher European defence spending, given the dislocation between its valuation and the growth ahead.

Rheinmetall: significant exposure to Germany, where greater fiscal headroom supports spending commitments. Order timing, execution and cash conversion remain central to the near-term debate, but GS believes the valuation gives insufficient credit to the demand trajectory.
Drax Group: Capital Markets Day expected to pitch a new business model. Rating remains Buy.

Eutelsat: forecasts updated for GS's satellite defence benefit framework and for estimate downgrades after disappointing FY27 guidance. Price target cut to EUR 1.6 from EUR 5.22. Near-term execution risk offsets longer-term defence upside. Rating remains Neutral.

market_movers.rationale: GS reinstates SES at Buy after the shares doubled and then halved within a year. C-band cash and higher space-defence spend offer asymmetric upside, with 79% upside to the target.

Rheinmetall (on the Conviction List) is the most compelling way to capture higher European defence spending. The valuation is dislocated from the growth opportunity, and Germany's fiscal headroom supports spending.
